purpose: Internal recommendations, not the live course manifest. Provider identifiers and syllabus evidence must not be rendered as public course copy.

referenceConventions.prerequisites: Same-class chapter IDs; priorClassReadiness describes the incoming prerequisite. Order is a teaching recommendation, not a requirement to lock every branch.
referenceConventions.sourceChapterIds: grade/chapter in the current production bank. A new course chapter can reuse an existing bank chapter; newChapter does not claim a generator exists.
referenceConventions.outcomes: Each object gives child-facing text and the existing, currently reachable families serving it. Empty families means an explicit content gap; proposedFormats are requirements, not implemented IDs.
referenceConventions.tools: Existing website paths. Tools support only their named skill; a calculator checks work, it does not teach a topic.
referenceConventions.games: IDs in gameCatalog; Space Academy must receive source grade/chapter and level, not a newly invented chapter ID.

S-level-1-weighting.caveat: Published note; not implemented merely by labelling an Explore/Reason/Stretch level. Achievers uses current-class section-2 topics.

CREST-readiness.coursePolicy: Reference only: PP1/PP2 remain untimed readiness, not exam tracks.

decisions: Retain the 56 production chapters; propose three additional teaching homes: PP2 time, Class 2 reasoning and Class 3 patterns. Only PP2 time and Class 2 reasoning require missing formats to become complete.

Do not call Class 4 decimals a published syllabus gap: neither fetched Class 4 topic list explicitly includes decimals. Decimal money appears in a CREST sample, so teach that within money; an optional decimal bridge is future enrichment.
Do not infer coverage from a skill label or frozen v1/v2 plan: bank3 overrides the live chapter-family routes.
Class 5 angles, symmetry, conversions, HCF/LCM, mirror clocks and restricted water-image tasks already exist. Expand weak formats rather than create duplicate chapters.
PP1/PP2 deliberately stay gentle. Missing provider ranges or literacy demands are reference differences, not permission to increase readiness difficulty.
Use all five chapter steps, but do not claim independent mastery on an outcome whose family list is empty.

classes.label: PP1
referenceDifferences: K1 names numbers 1-50 and number names 1-20; current production mostly stays within 20 and pp1-num-name is not a number-name literacy family.
All seven K1 shapes, including heart, star and oval, are present across PP1 levels.

chapters.title: Count with me
chapters.parentLine: Touch each object once, then connect a small group to its number.

outcomes.text: I can count a small group.
I can match a group to a number.
I can find the next number.

chapters.title: More, less and the same
chapters.parentLine: Compare groups and everyday sizes without racing.

outcomes.text: I can find more or fewer objects.
I can compare big, tall and thick things.
I can compare weight and how full a jar is.

chapters.title: Meet the shapes
chapters.parentLine: Name familiar outlines and notice corners and matching shapes.

outcomes.text: I can match a shape.
I can notice sides and corners.
I can find a shape in a picture.

chapters.title: Which ones belong?
chapters.parentLine: Sort familiar things by one visible rule before combining clues.

outcomes.text: I can find things that belong together.
I can find the one that is different.
I can count just one group.

chapters.title: Where is it?
chapters.parentLine: Use position words with toys, pictures and simple rows.

outcomes.text: I can find what is inside or outside.
I can find what is above or below.
I can find a place in a row.

chapters.title: What comes next?
chapters.parentLine: Say the repeating group aloud and continue a picture pattern.

outcomes.text: I can continue a picture pattern.
I can find a missing picture.
I can notice how a pattern grows.

classes.label: PP2
classes.priorClassReadiness: Count and compare small groups; recognise basic shapes.
referenceDifferences: K2 number names 1-50 are not covered by the current <=20 numeric bank.
K2 days/months and its inline clock sample have no PP2 chapter route; add an untimed teaching home, not a formal paper.
Oval recognition and explicit thick/thin and position-word assessment need PP2 variants; PP1 families are not automatically routed to PP2.

chapters.title: Numbers up to 20
chapters.parentLine: Build a ten, count the loose ones and find neighbours.

outcomes.text: I can show numbers up to 20.
I can find before, after and between.
I can compare numbers and skip-count.

proposedFormats: Optional spoken/written number-to-word matching; keep independent readiness checks within 20.

chapters.title: Add and take away
chapters.parentLine: Join groups, remove objects and find a hidden part.

outcomes.text: I can add two small groups.
I can find what is left.
I can find a missing part.

chapters.title: Flat shapes and solid things
chapters.parentLine: Connect shapes to real objects and simple position clues.

outcomes.text: I can count sides and corners.
I can recognise a solid by how it moves.
I can join shapes to make a picture.

chapters.title: Long, heavy and full
chapters.parentLine: Compare objects with common units and informal balances.

outcomes.text: I can compare lengths and sizes.
I can measure with equal blocks.
I can compare weight and capacity.

chapters.title: Find the pattern
chapters.parentLine: Repeat a group, fill a gap and predict a growing picture.

outcomes.text: I can continue a repeating group.
I can fill a gap in a pattern.
I can spot a broken rule.

chapters.title: Follow the picture clues
chapters.parentLine: Use positions, arrows and two visible clues.

outcomes.text: I can find a place in a row.
I can choose a picture using two clues.
I can follow arrows on a map.

chapters.title: Days, months and clocks
chapters.parentLine: Talk about daily routines, weekday order and whole hours together.

outcomes.text: I can say the day before or after.
I can put familiar months in order.
I can recognise a whole hour on a clock.

proposedFormats: Spoken weekday sequencing with picture choices
Match whole-hour clocks to a daily routine
chapters.practicePolicy: Clock Master is adult-guided reinforcement. Do not send an unsupported pp2/time ID to Space Academy; add grade-specific families before enabling scored Practise/Print/Check.

classes.label: Class 1
classes.priorClassReadiness: Represent numbers to 20; add and remove small groups; follow a picture pattern.

chapters.title: Tens, ones and number names
chapters.parentLine: Connect two-digit numerals, words, blocks and number order.

outcomes.text: I can build a number with tens and ones.
I can match a number to its name.
I can compare and order two-digit numbers.

chapters.title: Add, subtract and find the missing part
chapters.parentLine: Use pictures and part-whole models before written calculations.

outcomes.text: I can solve an add or take-away story.
I can find a missing part.
I can check related number facts.

chapters.title: Picture and number patterns
chapters.parentLine: Notice repeating groups and equal jumps, then explain the rule.

outcomes.text: I can fill a missing picture.
I can continue a growing pattern.
I can find a missing number or letter.

chapters.title: Shapes and solid objects
chapters.parentLine: Name flat and solid shapes and describe visible properties.

outcomes.text: I can count shapes and corners.
I can choose a solid by what it does.
I can complete a simple mirror picture.

chapters.title: Measure length and weight
chapters.parentLine: Compare fairly and measure with units that stay the same size.

outcomes.text: I can measure with equal units.
I can compare weights.
I can choose a sensible unit.

chapters.title: Read clocks and calendars
chapters.parentLine: Read the hands first, then connect times and calendar order.

outcomes.text: I can read a clock.
I can find a later time.
I can find a day or month.

chapters.title: Coins, prices and change
chapters.parentLine: Read coin values, add prices and find what comes back.

outcomes.text: I can add coin values.
I can total two prices.
I can work out my change.

chapters.title: Sort, order and solve picture clues
chapters.parentLine: Use every clue to group objects, follow positions and transfer a rule.

outcomes.text: I can find what does not belong.
I can find someone's place in a row.
I can follow a picture change or route.

classes.label: Class 2
classes.priorClassReadiness: Understand tens/ones, add/subtract, read familiar clock times and simple patterns.

chapters.title: Hundreds, tens and ones
chapters.parentLine: Build, compare and name three-digit numbers.

outcomes.text: I can read hundreds, tens and ones.
I can order and compare numbers.
I can match a three-digit number to its written name.

proposedFormats: Three-digit numeral to full written name and inverse, including zero tens; place-words currently composes numeric hundreds/tens/ones, not full written names.

chapters.title: Add, subtract and make equal groups
chapters.parentLine: Connect three-digit calculations to arrays and missing-part stories.

outcomes.text: I can add and subtract in a story.
I can count equal groups.
I can find a missing digit or amount.

chapters.gameScope: Math Tank only for taught multiplication/division facts, not regrouping or word problems.

chapters.title: Find number and picture rules
chapters.parentLine: Separate number sequences from the trickier reasoning formats.

outcomes.text: I can continue a number series.
I can continue a growing picture.
I can use the same rule for a new number.

chapters.title: Lines, shapes and solids
chapters.parentLine: Count carefully, describe solids and recognise reflected shapes.

outcomes.text: I can count lines and shapes.
I can describe a solid.
I can complete a reflected picture.

chapters.title: Length, weight, capacity and temperature
chapters.parentLine: Read everyday scales and choose units that match the quantity.

outcomes.text: I can measure and compare lengths.
I can compare weight and capacity.
I can compare thermometer readings.

chapters.title: Clocks, dates and how long
chapters.parentLine: Read a clock, use a calendar and follow short timetables.

outcomes.text: I can match a clock to a time.
I can work out how long something takes.
I can use a calendar or timetable.

chapters.title: Shop, save and find change
chapters.parentLine: Read a price board and track money spent and left.

outcomes.text: I can make an amount with notes and coins.
I can find a missing price or change.
I can compare purchases within a budget.

chapters.title: Read picture charts
chapters.parentLine: Use a key before comparing or adding chart values.

outcomes.text: I can use a pictograph key.
I can compare chart values.
I can check a statement about data.

chapters.title: Codes, hidden shapes and order
chapters.parentLine: Give the reasoning syllabus a clear home instead of hiding it in patterns.

outcomes.text: I can group pictures and use an analogy.
I can use a code key to read a message.
I can find an exact shape hidden in a picture.
I can find a place in a row.

proposedFormats: Restore grade-appropriate code-key/code-infer reachability; include digit-symbol and letter-code variants
Exact embedded-line figure selection with rotation policy stated; hidden-shape counting is not equivalent
chapters.practicePolicy: Until live reasoning routing exists, link its listed source chapters and do not claim the two unsupported outcomes are mastered.

classes.label: Class 3
classes.priorClassReadiness: Use three-digit place value; know small equal-group facts and scaled pictographs.

chapters.title: Thousands and number names
chapters.parentLine: Read four-digit numbers and use place-value clues.

outcomes.text: I can build and name a four-digit number.
I can order and round numbers.
I can solve a number clue.

chapters.title: Multiply, divide and solve stories
chapters.parentLine: Connect arrays and sharing to written methods and two-step problems.

outcomes.text: I can multiply and share equally.
I can find a missing digit.
I can choose operations for a story.

chapters.title: Equal parts and fractions
chapters.parentLine: Use the same whole when reading, comparing and finding fractions.

outcomes.text: I can read a shaded fraction.
I can compare equal fractions.
I can find a fraction of a group.

chapters.title: Shapes, reflections and boundaries
chapters.parentLine: Describe shapes, follow reflections and measure a boundary.

outcomes.text: I can describe flat and solid shapes.
I can find symmetry and mirror images.
I can find a shape's boundary length.

chapters.title: Read scales and change units

outcomes.text: I can read a ruler or thermometer.
I can compare mass and capacity.
I can combine mixed units.

chapters.title: Time, timetables and dates
chapters.parentLine: Read clock hands, cross an hour boundary and use calendar intervals.

outcomes.text: I can read and choose clocks.
I can work out elapsed time.
I can use dates and timetables.

chapters.title: Shopping totals and better buys
chapters.parentLine: Track quantities as well as prices when comparing purchases.

outcomes.text: I can total prices and find change.
I can compare pack prices.
I can choose within a budget.

chapters.title: Picture charts, bars and tables
chapters.parentLine: Read the key or scale before comparing several results.

outcomes.text: I can use a picture-chart key.
I can compare values on a bar chart.
I can update a table or chart.

chapters.title: Number, letter and picture patterns
chapters.parentLine: Make the existing pattern families easy to find before complex logic.

outcomes.text: I can complete a number series.
I can complete a letter pattern.
I can copy a picture rule.

syllabusTopics: Grouping of Figures and Figure Matrix
chapters.practicePolicy: Navigation split only; use class-3/reasoning until a dedicated bank route is implemented.

chapters.title: Codes, positions and picture puzzles
chapters.parentLine: Use codes and ordering clues, then explain why all clues fit.

outcomes.text: I can use a code or word clue.
I can find ranks and allowed combinations.
I can find a hidden letter and follow directions.

proposedFormats: Broaden embedded-letter tasks to exact non-letter line figures; direction sense is enrichment here, not explicitly named in the fetched Class 3 list.

classes.label: Class 4
classes.priorClassReadiness: Use four-digit numbers and four operations; understand equal fractions and scale intervals.

chapters.title: Bigger numbers, factors and Roman numerals
chapters.parentLine: Use place value beyond four digits and investigate exact groups.

outcomes.text: I can build and compare larger numbers.
I can find factors and multiples.
I can read and use Roman numerals.
I can match a five-digit number to its written name.

proposedFormats: Five-digit numeral to full written name and inverse, with zero places. Existing words-place reads full words only in a four-digit subtraction variant.

chapters.title: Calculate and solve step by step
chapters.parentLine: Choose operations, use written methods and check missing information.

outcomes.text: I can multiply and divide using models.
I can interpret a remainder.
I can solve a linked story or missing digit.

chapters.title: Compare and use fractions
chapters.parentLine: Keep track of the whole while matching parts and solving changes.

outcomes.text: I can show equal fractions.
I can find a fraction of an amount.
I can find what is left after fraction changes.

chapters.title: Perimeter, area and symmetry
chapters.parentLine: Separate the outside boundary from the space inside a shape.

outcomes.text: I can find a perimeter or missing side.
I can find area using square units.
I can complete a reflection or folded solid.

chapters.title: Measure and convert units
chapters.parentLine: Read the scale and convert length, mass or capacity before calculating.

outcomes.text: I can measure from a non-zero mark.
I can combine or share mixed units.
I can use balances and temperature scales.

chapters.title: Timetables, dates and clock errors
chapters.parentLine: Use intervals and distinguish the clock reading from the true time.

outcomes.text: I can find a missing time interval.
I can use a timetable or calendar.

chapters.gameScope: Clock Master reinforces reading hands, not calendar arithmetic or clock-error puzzles.

chapters.title: Bills, budgets and rupees with paise
chapters.parentLine: Keep rupees and paise lined up while comparing real shopping choices.

outcomes.text: I can total a bill and find change.
I can compare equal amounts in packs.
I can choose within a budget.

chapters.note: No separate required decimals chapter is inferred from decimal currency notation.

chapters.title: Read scaled charts and compare results
chapters.parentLine: Use axes, half-symbol keys and totals across displays.

outcomes.text: I can use a non-unit chart scale.

I can compare and update survey data.

chapters.title: Codes, turns and hidden pictures
chapters.parentLine: Explain each code, picture or ordering rule before selecting an answer.

outcomes.text: I can use codes and alphabet order.
I can follow turns and ranking clues.
I can find a hidden figure or picture rule.
I can list possible pairs without missing any.

proposedFormats: Restore constrained pair/menu combinations to live Class 4 reasoning; route-counting alone is not the same format.

classes.label: Class 5
classes.priorClassReadiness: Use larger whole numbers, four operations, equivalent fractions and mixed measurement units.

chapters.title: Large numbers and place-value clues
chapters.parentLine: Build towards seven- and eight-digit values using place value and number words.

outcomes.text: I can build and compare numbers up to seven digits.
I can round and solve digit clues.
I can use Roman numerals.
I can read and name an eight-digit number.

proposedFormats: Add eight-digit number construction, comparison and place-value chart including the crore column; current core families cap at seven digits.
Add explicit full written-name matching for large numbers; place-value representations alone do not prove name literacy.

chapters.title: Solve stories with factors and multiples
chapters.parentLine: Choose a method, use exact groups or repeating schedules, and check the result.

outcomes.text: I can solve a linked calculation story.
I can find common factors and multiples.
I can use a repeating schedule and interpret leftovers.

proposedFormats: Add equal-packet and greatest-equal-length HCF stories; current HCF mix is mostly numerical, while LCM already has meet-again applications.

chapters.title: Fractions, mixed numbers and what is left
chapters.parentLine: Connect pictures and quantities before solving repeated changes.

outcomes.text: I can match equivalent and mixed fractions.
I can order fractions and find a fraction of an amount.
I can find what is left after fraction changes.

proposedFormats: More Explore whole shapes, number-line intervals and inverse shading; do not rely on new numbers in one bar template.

chapters.title: Tenths, hundredths and decimal calculations
chapters.parentLine: Connect fractions and place value, then line up decimal places.

outcomes.text: I can show decimals on a grid or line.
I can compare decimals and link them to fractions.
I can calculate decimal money and measures.

chapters.title: Angles, symmetry, perimeter and area
chapters.parentLine: Name the measurement needed before using shape facts.

outcomes.text: I can find a perimeter or area.
I can use angle facts.
I can complete symmetry or fold a cube net.

proposedFormats: Count parallel/perpendicular line pairs with orientation distractors, as distinct from angle chasing; add more exact hidden-shape choices.

chapters.title: Convert and compare measurements
chapters.parentLine: Read scales and convert length, mass or capacity before calculating.

outcomes.text: I can read a dial or thermometer.
I can compare mixed units.
I can solve a measurement story and estimate sensibly.

chapters.title: Elapsed time, timetables and dates
chapters.parentLine: Separate actual time, displayed time and calendar intervals.

outcomes.text: I can find elapsed time.
I can correct clock errors and switch time formats.
I can use a calendar and timetable.

chapters.gameScope: Clock Master only supports reading hands; use Space Academy for calendar, timetable and error reasoning.

chapters.title: Plan a budget and compare value
chapters.parentLine: Compare like quantities and account for every price change.

outcomes.text: I can total purchases and find missing prices.
I can compare value for money.
I can check a budget after a discount.

chapters.title: Charts, averages and true statements
chapters.parentLine: Read the scale, combine results and justify a claim.

outcomes.text: I can read pictographs and scaled bars.
I can compare two displays or a line graph.
I can find an average and check a chart statement.

chapters.title: Codes, reflections and logic puzzles
chapters.parentLine: Test every clue and distinguish turning, mirroring and flipping.

outcomes.text: I can use codes, series and ranking clues.
I can follow directions and count combinations.
I can reason about mirror clocks and reflected words.
I can order words by their logical meaning.
I can find an exact shape hidden inside a figure.

proposedFormats: Meaning-based sequence-of-words choices, not just alphabetical or person ordering
Exact embedded figure and NOT-embedded choices with a stated rotation rule
Non-letter mirror/water-image picture choices; current water coverage is restricted self-symmetric words
